title: Rule Timing During a Reconstructed Retracement

data_provenance.text: This lesson reuses the repository's local aggregate-observation fixture and makes no real-market identity claim.
The event-by-event market path and all Level 2 behavior are deterministic synthetic reconstruction.

historical_context.text: The same aggregate teaching constraints are viewed through a rule-confirmation and invalidation lens.
Observable imbalance, depletion, and spread sequences come from the selected reconstruction and may differ from any unavailable historical path.

learning_objectives: Distinguish setup formation, confirmation, invalidation, and cooldown timing.
Evaluate whether traffic-light rules respond too early or too slowly to observable flow.
Keep rule evaluation conditional on the synthetic scenario rather than treating it as historical proof.

event.text: A directional aggregate teaching pattern included a brief retracement before the configured close.

market_context.text: Rule inputs were computed from one generated queue path constrained only by the disclosed aggregate fixture.

what_happened_next.text: The selected reconstruction resumed directional flow after its synthetic retracement and ended at its generated book state.

why_session_matters.text: It exposes rule latency and invalidation tradeoffs without pretending the unseen historical order sequence is known.

known_limitations: Historical Level 2 is missing; rule inputs reflect synthetic reconstruction rather than recovered historical queues.
The source fixture is pedagogical and locally authored, so no real instrument event is asserted.
A different deterministic reconstruction seed could produce another path consistent with similar aggregate constraints.
training_questions: Did your traffic-light rules react too slowly?
Which observable confirmed the setup, and which invalidated it?
Would the conclusion survive a different reconstruction path?
